steps.title: Open the Data Manager
steps.narration: Start on the Data Manager page, where an operator can grow the dataset on demand and see exactly what every past job did.
steps.point_out: Four panels are visible — Dataset coverage, the job submission form, Job progress, and Run history with real past runs already listed.

steps.title: Enter the start of a May 2026 range
steps.narration: Type in a start date from May 2026 — a month that used to get silently skipped by backfill requests.
steps.point_out: The Start date field now holds 2026-05-02.

steps.title: Enter the end of the range
steps.narration: Add an end date to complete the range, covering nearly a full month.
steps.point_out: The End date field now holds 2026-05-29.

steps.title: Run the backfill
steps.narration: Submit the job. Ranges like this used to report success while quietly doing nothing — now the app tells you exactly what happened.
steps.point_out: The status badge, and the plain-English breakdown line underneath it: calendar days, non-trading days, and how many were already covered.

steps.title: Try a weekend-only start date
steps.narration: Now try a range that's only a Saturday — no trading days in it at all.
steps.point_out: The Start date field holds 2026-05-02 again.

steps.title: Try a weekend-only end date
steps.narration: Finish the range with the following Sunday.

steps.title: Submit the weekend range
steps.narration: Submit this zero-trading-day range and see how the app now handles it.
steps.point_out: A distinct grey "no new snapshots" badge, plus a note box explaining every requested day was already covered or wasn't a trading day — never mistaken for a normal successful run.

steps.title: Reload the page
steps.narration: Refresh the browser entirely, as if starting a brand-new visit.
steps.point_out: Run history is still right there, including the jobs just submitted — nothing resets to a blank slate.

steps.title: Enter a start date after the end date
steps.narration: Type in a start date that's actually later than the end date, to check the app still catches this mistake.

steps.title: Enter an end date before the start date
steps.narration: Add an end date that comes before it.

steps.title: Submit the invalid range
steps.narration: Try to submit this backwards range. Even though much larger ranges are now accepted, basic checks like date order still hold.
steps.point_out: A red error message explaining the start date must be on or before the end date — the job is never submitted.

steps.title: Open Scanner Runs
steps.narration: Head over to the Scanner Runs page, which lists every daily snapshot the system has ever produced.
steps.point_out: New dates from May 2026 now appear in the list — dates that only exist because that backfill actually ran.

steps.title: Open the May 4 scanner run
steps.narration: Open one of those new runs to see the full daily snapshot it created.
steps.point_out: A regime badge and a populated table of stocks for that day — a real, immutable snapshot, not an empty page.

steps.title: Head back to the Data Manager
steps.narration: Return to the Data Manager page for one more request.
steps.point_out: The same four panels as before.

steps.title: Enter a start date over a decade back
steps.narration: This time, ask for a much bigger range — the kind of request that used to be rejected outright for being too large.

steps.title: Enter an end date over a year later
steps.narration: Set the end date more than 370 days after the start — well past the old limit.

steps.title: Submit the large range
steps.narration: Submit this long-span request and watch it actually get accepted.
steps.point_out: The job starts running immediately, and a "chunk N of M" badge appears — the range is processed in manageable pieces instead of being rejected.
